targetText: The Commune, therefore, appears to have replaced the smashed state machine “only” by fuller democracy: abolition of the standing army; all officials to be elected and subject to recall.
summary: Analyzing the 1871 Paris Commune, Lenin explains how workers replaced the repressive capitalist state with real proletarian democracy: abolishing the professional army, electing all public servants, and making them subject to immediate recall.
context: Marx and Engels considered the Paris Commune of 1871 the first historical example of the dictatorship of the proletariat, highlighting its radical measures to prevent bureaucratic self-interest.

targetText: The Commune was to be a working, not a parliamentary, body, executive and legislative at the same time.
summary: Lenin contrasts proletarian democracy against bourgeois parliamentarism, stressing that representative institutions under workers' power must directly execute laws rather than functioning as corrupt talking shops.
